ablations.prompt: Explain inflation to a 10-year-old. Use 3 bullet points.

runs.answer:
- Inflation means prices slowly go up over time. A candy bar that cost 50 cents when your grandparents were kids might cost a dollar or more today.

- Your money buys less than it used to. If you have $5 saved, it can get you fewer things next year than it does now, because the same items cost more.

- Governments and banks watch inflation closely. A little bit of it is normal and happens most years, but if prices rise too fast, it can make life harder for families.

- **Inflation is when prices go up.** Something that cost $1 last year might cost $1.05 this year, so the same money buys a little less stuff.

- **Why it happens:** Sometimes lots of people want to buy the same things, or it costs more to make them. When there's more demand for toys than there are toys, stores can charge more.

- **Why it matters:** If your allowance stays the same but candy and video games get more expensive, you can afford less candy and fewer games than you could before, even though you still have the same dollars.
